texts: In the Crawford classification as extended by Safi, a type V aneurysm begins in the mid-thoracic aorta, below the sixth intercostal space, and ends at the renal arteries: E.
In the picture, baby V sets off halfway down the chest and stops at the kidney beans.
Type I runs from the left subclavian artery to above the renal arteries, and type II, the most extensive, from the left subclavian artery to the aortic bifurcation.
Type III begins at the same mid-thoracic level but goes on below the renal arteries, the baby that crawls past the beans; type IV begins at the diaphragm and takes in the abdominal aorta.
Memory hook: baby V starts halfway down the chest and stops at the kidney beans.
